text: Bring federal dollars home to CA-45 communities.
House appropriators advanced more than $14 million for 15 of his community projects (Jul 2025).
Delivered $3.15 million for the Del Amo Boulevard bridge in Cerritos.
Secured $1 million for Garden Grove firefighters.
Delivered $1 million to Cypress for flood prevention.
Presented $850,000 to the Buena Park Library District.
Delivered $925,000 for public safety in Artesia.
GKN Aerospace chemical leak in Garden Grove: demanded answers from GKN with Rep. Robert Garcia (May 2026).
Introduced H.R. 10108, the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act (Aug 2026).
Issued a statement on GKN's $125 million settlement (Oct 2026).
“small businesses are the backbone of our economy”
quote: small businesses are the backbone of our economy

text: His bill H.R. 5788 (504 Program Risk Oversight Act) passed the House on Jan 20, 2026, and was sent to the Senate.
Cosponsored H.R. 787 (Plain Language in Contracting Act), which passed the House in June 2025.
Ranking Member of the Small Business oversight subcommittee.
Protect veterans' jobs and benefits and keep a strong national defense.
Cosponsored the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102), which passed the House 392–18 on Nov 12, 2026.
Voted yes on the final FY26 NDAA (Dec 10, 2025), citing the 3.8% troop pay raise. He had voted no on the House version in September.
His first bill, H.R. 1637 (Protect Veteran Jobs Act), has had no action since it was introduced on Feb 26, 2025.
Oppose cuts to Social Security and Medicare.
Voted no on H.R. 1 (May 22 and Jul 3, 2025).
Voted for H.R. 5348 (Social Security Child Protection Act), which passed 386–0 on Dec 1, 2025.
Introduced H.R. 6678 (Senior Legal Hotline Act). Held town halls in Cerritos, Buena Park and Westminster.
Stand firm against Chinese Communist rule and push for human rights in Vietnam.
Introduced Black April resolutions (2025 and 2026), a Vietnamese Heritage Flag resolution and H.R. 7969 (Combating CCP Influence Act).
Got an appropriations amendment passed to fund the U.S.–Vietnam Human Rights Dialogue (Jul 2026).
Wrote letters about prisoners of conscience, including journalist Le Huu Minh Tuan, and announced a State Department response in Oct 2026.
Lower costs for families, with tax cuts for middle-class families and small businesses.
Co-founded the Lowering Costs Caucus with Reps. Landsman and Scholten (Jun 2025).
Introduced H.R. 4746 (Baby Food Tax Relief Act). Cosponsored the Toll of Tariffs Act, Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act and Stop the Trump Electricity Price Hikes Act.
“healthcare should be a right, not a privilege”
quote: healthcare should be a right, not a privilege

text: Voted no on both House votes on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Medicaid and ACA cuts), which passed anyway.
Cosponsored H.R. 4849 to make enhanced ACA credits permanent. He voted Yea when a 3-year extension (H.R. 1834) passed the House 230–196 on Jan 8, 2026.
Voted no on funding bills that let ACA credits lapse.
“ensure that all workers can afford housing”
quote: ensure that all workers can afford housing

text: Introduced H.R. 10613 (Housing COST Act, Sep 2026). Cosponsored the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act.
Delivered $250K for affordable housing in Orange. Urged the President to sign the ROAD to Housing Act.
Oppose mass deportations, support reform with a path to citizenship, and hold ICE accountable.
Introduced H.R. 9883 (Private Detention Corporate Accountability Act). Cosponsored ICE and CBP accountability bills. All remain in committee.
Voted no on DHS funding without ICE reforms (Jan–Mar 2026), per his office.
Voted for the Laken Riley Act (Jan 22, 2025), breaking with most Democrats.
“Derek will fight to end this culture of corruption in our politics.”
quote: Derek will fight to end this culture of corruption in our politics.

text: Cosponsored stock-trading bans H.R. 7852 (No Getting Rich in Congress Act) and STOCK Act 2.0.
Voted for the Epstein Files Transparency Act (passed 427–1, Nov 18, 2025).
Voted for the Republican-led Stop Insider Trading Act (H.R. 7008), which passed 232–198 on Jul 22, 2026. Democrats opposed it 13–198.
Codify a national right to abortion care.
Cosponsored H.R. 12 (Women's Health Protection Act), the Right to IVF Act and the Stop Comstock Act.
Whether he signed the 2026 petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act II, which reached 218 signatures, is not confirmed. None of his 265 press releases mention Epstein.
Related: voted to make the House Ethics Committee release records of sexual-harassment settlements involving members (H.Res. 1399, passed unanimously).
Related: voted against sending a resolution to release House sexual-harassment records back to committee, breaking with most Democrats (182–27 to refer).
Voted for the Epstein Files Transparency Act (H.R. 4405), requiring the Justice Department to release its Epstein files. It passed 427–1.
Voted against a Republican resolution to censure Del. Stacey Plaskett over texting with Jeffrey Epstein during a 2019 hearing. It failed 209–214.
Signed the Massie-Khanna discharge petition that forced the House vote. NBC News reported that all House Democrats signed it; his individual signature was not checked against the Clerk's list.
Voted yes on the Deporting Fraudsters Act (H.R. 1958). “Cheating the government and stealing public benefits threatens the stability of the entire system.”
quote: Cheating the government and stealing public benefits threatens the stability of the entire system.

text: Voted no on H.R. 7148, the package that ended the partial shutdown, over ICE funding without reforms. Also voted no on DHS bills in March 2026. “I will not be complicit in the wrongful targeting and killing of American citizens.”
quote: I will not be complicit in the wrongful targeting and killing of American citizens.

text: Cosponsored articles of impeachment against DHS Secretary Kristi Noem (H.Res. 996) after federal agents killed two people in Minneapolis. “No one is above the law, especially those who are entrusted with enforcing it.”
quote: No one is above the law, especially those who are entrusted with enforcing it.

text: Criticized ICE raids at a Buena Park press conference. “focus on violent criminals, not law-abiding community members.”
quote: focus on violent criminals, not law-abiding community members.

text: Opposed the National Guard deployment to LA after visiting the Adelanto ICE facility. “President Trump's unnecessary and premature deployment of the National Guard will create more fear and suppress free speech.”
quote: President Trump's unnecessary and premature deployment of the National Guard will create more fear and suppress free speech.

text: Voted yes on the Laken Riley Act, one of 46 House Democrats to do so. “I voted to ensure that those committing crimes, no matter their immigration status, are held to a standard of justice.”
quote: I voted to ensure that those committing crimes, no matter their immigration status, are held to a standard of justice.

text: State of the Union response: said the President offered no plan to lower costs and doubled down on tariffs. “put people over politics.”
Helped introduce the Toll of Tariffs Act to measure what tariffs cost families. “President Trump's reckless trade wars are taking a toll on working families' wallets.”
quote: President Trump's reckless trade wars are taking a toll on working families' wallets.

text: Cosponsored H.R. 4849 to make enhanced ACA premium tax credits permanent; signed the Hands Off Medicaid and SNAP discharge petition.

Voted no on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, citing Medicaid cuts and his family's past reliance on Medicaid, SNAP and Section 8. “My constituents sent me to Congress to fight for lower costs and safer communities.”
quote: My constituents sent me to Congress to fight for lower costs and safer communities.

text: Voted yes on H.R. 6500, a stopgap funding the government through Dec 11, 2026, calling it a temporary fix.
Voted against the bill that ended the fall 2025 shutdown (passed 222–209).
Blamed Republicans for the fall 2025 shutdown; original cosponsor of the bipartisan Pay Our Troops Act. “I will never vote for a bill that harms the people of California's 45th district.”
quote: I will never vote for a bill that harms the people of California's 45th district.

text: Voted present on tabling a Trump impeachment resolution, with 47 other Democrats, instead of voting to advance it. “It is clear that President Trump must be held accountable for his abuse of power.”
quote: It is clear that President Trump must be held accountable for his abuse of power.

text: At Cerritos and Buena Park town halls, promoted his Protect Veteran Jobs Act to reinstate veterans fired by DOGE.
Co-led a 65-member letter to Secretary Rubio on Israeli dual-use restrictions blocking aid to Gaza.

Voted for the Massie amendment to end FY2027 military aid to Israel, while backing continued Iron Dome funding. It failed 104–314; House Democrats split 103–98 in favor. “I supported Representative Massie's amendment to end unconditional funding for Israel.”
quote: I supported Representative Massie's amendment to end unconditional funding for Israel.

text: Voted for the Iran War Powers Resolution (H.Con.Res. 86), which passed 215–208.
Cosponsors the Block the Bombs Act (H.R. 3565), which would restrict certain munitions transfers to Israel.
Opposed the U.S. strike on Iran's nuclear sites as carried out without Congress's approval. “We cannot afford another endless war.”
quote: We cannot afford another endless war.

text: Voted against H.R. 23, the ICC sanctions bill (passed 243–140).
Introduced a bicameral bill with Sen. Blumenthal to block future VA cuts to disabled veterans' health care, after a VA rule was reversed.
Passed an appropriations amendment funding the U.S.–Vietnam Human Rights Dialogue.

Criticized the Trump trade deal with Vietnam over human rights; co-leads the Vietnam Human Rights Act (H.R. 3122). “President Trump is ignoring the gross human rights abuses taking place under the leadership of the communist government.”
quote: President Trump is ignoring the gross human rights abuses taking place under the leadership of the communist government.

text: Cosponsors the Women's Health Protection Act (H.R. 12) and voted against two GOP reproductive health bills.
Voted for the bipartisan Combating Organized Retail Crime Act (H.R. 2853).
No public statement found on Prop 50, which redrew CA-45 to take in more of Los Angeles County, including parts of Lakewood.
Co-led a letter from 65 members urging Secretary Rubio to ease Israeli “dual-use” restrictions blocking humanitarian aid to Gaza.
Voted for the Massie amendment to cut $3.3B in military aid to Israel, saying he wants to “end unconditional funding for Israel.”
In the same statement, said he supports continued funding for Israel's defense, including Iron Dome.
Hosted CAIR-LA's Hussam Ayloush at his Capitol office during Muslim Advocacy Day; Republicans attacked him for it.
Took a J Street Education Fund trip to Israel (Feb 13–20, 2026, $19,864) to “explore the current situation in Israel” and the Palestinian territories. J Street backs Israel and a two-state solution.
Cosponsors H.R. 3565, which would restrict transfers of certain bombs to Israel.
Gave a floor speech saying Israel was killing Palestinians seeking aid, as reported by the Washington Free Beacon. The exact wording is unverified.
Called a nuclear Iran dangerous to the U.S. and Israel, while urging diplomacy over military strikes.
Voted against H.R. 23, the bill to sanction the International Criminal Court after it issued warrants for Israeli leaders.
Took about $220,000 from pro-Israel groups, almost all through J Street, and $0 from AIPAC's PAC. Endorsed by J Street, not AIPAC.
Introduced H.R. 9883, the Private Detention Corporate Accountability Act, setting a $5M minimum payout for wrongful deaths in private ICE detention.
Voted for H.R. 1689 to grant Temporary Protected Status to Haitians.
Voted “Present” on H.Res. 1128, which backed full DHS funding and thanked DHS staff including ICE. Most Democrats voted no (9–187).
Voted for the Deporting Fraudsters Act (H.R. 1958), breaking with most Democrats.
Voted against DHS appropriations (H.R. 7744) because it funded ICE without reforms.
Voted against the final funding package (H.R. 7148): “I will not be complicit in the wrongful targeting and killing of American citizens.”
Cosponsored articles of impeachment against DHS Secretary Kristi Noem (H.Res. 996).
Joined 14 other veterans in Congress demanding ICE and CBP stand down after federal agents killed two people in Minneapolis.
Voted against the Kayla Hamilton Act (H.R. 4371).
Voted against the Stop Illegal Entry Act (H.R. 3486), saying it “will only sow more division.”
Voted against H.R. 875, which makes DUI grounds for deportation.
Said of the Southern California raids: “what ICE is doing right now is not making us safer.”
Voted for H.Res. 488, which “expresses gratitude to law enforcement officers, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement personnel.” Most Democrats voted no (75–113).
Opposed the National Guard deployment to Los Angeles during the immigration raids.
Voted against the Agent Raul Gonzalez Officer Safety Act (H.R. 35), which raised penalties for fleeing Border Patrol.
Voted for the Preventing Violence Against Women by Illegal Aliens Act (H.R. 30), breaking with most Democrats.
Voted for the Laken Riley Act, which requires ICE to detain immigrants charged with theft. He was one of 46 Democrats.
Voted for the Cashless Bail Reporting Act (H.R. 5625); most Democrats voted no (96–114).
Voted for H.Res. 1252 memorializing officers killed in the line of duty.
Voted against H.Con.Res. 96, a pro-police resolution whose preamble attacked “progressive politicians” and sanctuary cities. Most Democrats voted no (29–173).
Voted for the Combating Organized Retail Crime Act (H.R. 2853).
Voted for the Law-Enforcement Innovate to De-Escalate Act (H.R. 2189), breaking with most Democrats.
Voted for the District of Columbia Policing Protection Act (H.R. 5143), breaking with most Democrats.
Voted for the DC CRIMES Act (H.R. 4922), breaking with most Democrats.
Voted against H.Res. 516 condemning the June 2025 Los Angeles riots. Most Democrats voted no (7–195).
Wrote to the Defense Secretary about the LA deployment: “Public safety will always be my top priority.”
Voted for H.R. 2240 on officer safety and wellness data.
Voted against H.R. 2255, which lets federal officers buy their retired service weapons.
Voted for H.Con.Res. 30 expressing support for local law enforcement officers.
Voted for the Retirement Fairness for Charities Act, which most Democrats opposed (83–128).
Led a bipartisan push with Rep. Anna Paulina Luna against shielding rideshare companies from liability lawsuits.
Introduced a bill holding private ICE detention companies liable for wrongful deaths (H.R. 9883).
Voted for the Main Street Act, the SHOWER Act on showerhead efficiency rules, the Affordable HOMES Act and the fuel retailer (E15) bill, all opposed by most Democrats.

Took $305,250 from 91 corporate PACs in 2025–26, such as Amazon, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Anduril, Coinbase and Walmart, plus law and accounting firms such as Deloitte and KPMG. In 2023–24 it was $0; four committees this page once counted as corporate were a union and advocacy groups. Counts use each committee's FEC type, then its name.
Took $137,507 from trade associations and cooperatives such as bankers, realtors, hospitals and sugar growers, up from $35,500 in 2023–24.
Voted for the Increasing Investor Opportunities Act, the DUMP Red Tape Act and the Electric Supply Chain Act, all opposed by most Democrats.
Voted for the Protect America's Workforce Act, restoring union rights for federal workers. Labor PACs gave him $196,500 in 2025–26.
Voted against the Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act and the Mining Regulatory Clarity Act.
Voted for the GENIUS Act and the CLARITY Act, the crypto industry's top bills. Most Democrats opposed CLARITY (78–134).
Voted against repealing consumer-protection rules on bank overdraft fees and big tech payment apps (S.J.Res. 18 and 28).
Voted for the repeal of the IRS rule requiring crypto platforms to report user transactions (H.J.Res. 25). Most Democrats voted no.
Voted against all 19 Republican resolutions in 2025 repealing environmental and energy rules.
Cosponsored the Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act and the Stop the Trump Electricity Price Hikes Act.

Pledged in his 2024 race: “I won’t accept a dime of corporate PAC money.” End Citizens United, which backs candidates who refuse it, gave his campaign $9,550 in 2023–24 and nothing in 2025–26 (FEC records).
Recruited into the DCCC's Red to Blue program in 2024 and its Frontline incumbent-protection program in 2025–26, and kept on Frontline after Prop 50 made his seat safer.

Jeffries campaigned for him in Anaheim (Oct 2024), held a joint event in Buena Park (Mar 2026) and endorsed him. Tran was one of five Democrats who formally nominated Jeffries for Speaker (Nov 18, 2026).

Money from party leaders' committees rose from $61,500 in 2023–24 to $135,759 in 2025–26. In 2024, four leadership PACs each gave $5,000 on Mar 28–29, the days the DCCC named him a Red to Blue candidate.
Member of the centrist New Democrat Coalition, endorsed by its Action Fund, and co-chair of the House Democratic Caucus National Security Task Force.
Party-aligned groups spent heavily for him in 2024: House Majority PAC spent $1.89 million supporting him, per FEC records, on top of its spending against Michelle Steel.
In his 2024 primary the California Democratic Party endorsed his rival, Kim Nguyen-Penaloza. He won by about 366 votes.
Voted for the Laken Riley Act and other Republican immigration bills, and for the resolution thanking ICE, against most Democrats.
Voted for the Massie amendment to cut $3.3B in military aid to Israel, which Jeffries opposed (Whip Clark and most Democrats voted yes).
Ranks 189 of 215 House Democrats for voting with his party.
Not a member of the Blue Dog Coalition or Problem Solvers Caucus. Also not in the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
One of five Democrats who formally nominate Jeffries for Speaker; urges “discipline” and “unity.”
FEC filings through Oct 14, 2026 show $305,250 from 91 corporate PACs in 2025–26, and $0 in 2023–24.
Votes for the Massie amendment to cut Israel military aid, which Jeffries opposed.
Hosts Jeffries in Buena Park for a veterans roundtable.
The Washington Free Beacon reports he took $46,500 from corporate PACs after pledging in his 2024 race not to take “a dime” of it.
Jeffries forms the Jeffries Battleground Protection Fund, which goes on to send Tran $56,942 in 2025–26.
Named co-chair of the House Democratic Caucus National Security Task Force.
Leads 66 House Democrats urging Senate leader Chuck Schumer to block the Republican funding bill, the same position as House leadership.
Named to the DCCC's Frontline program for vulnerable incumbents.
Votes for Jeffries for Speaker.
In the 2024 general election, House Majority PAC spends $1.89 million supporting him, while the Republican Congressional Leadership Fund spends $11.36 million against him, per FEC records.
Hakeem Jeffries campaigns for him at Golden Sea Restaurant in Anaheim, near Little Saigon.
DMFI PAC (Democratic Majority for Israel) endorses him for the general election.
End Citizens United endorses him for refusing corporate PAC money.
Within two days, the leadership PACs of Jeffries, Clark, Aguilar and Hoyer each give him $5,000, per FEC records.
DCCC adds him to Red to Blue, its program for top recruits.
California Democratic Party endorses his primary rival, Kim Nguyen-Penaloza.
Not a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus. Nearby Rep. Dave Min (CA-47) is.
No endorsement, criticism or primary challenge from Justice Democrats, Our Revolution, the Working Families Party, Sunrise or DSA was found. He had no progressive challenger in 2026.
MoveOn and J Street endorsed him in 2024.

Issued a statement praising Jeffries' election as the Democratic nominee for Speaker (Nov 18, 2026).
2024: UDP's only California House spending was in CA-34 and CA-47. In CA-47 it spent over $4 million, mostly on TV and mailers, against Dave Min before the March primary. Min won anyway.
2026: FEC independent-expenditure records show no UDP spending for or against Tran. UDP's California money this cycle went to the CA-14 race.
In 2023–24, AIPAC's PAC gave $19,512 to his Republican opponent, Michelle Steel, and nothing to Tran (total of the itemized gifts dated 2023 and 2024).
Track AIPAC's figure for Tran counts money from pro-Israel donors and PACs; FEC records show most of it came through J Street. It is not UDP spending.
